description: Eval cases for the repoGolem launcher skill. Tests correct launcher usage, flag mapping, interactive vs headless mode, and cmux integration. All from real violations in orc sessions.

evals.prompt: I need to spawn a Codex agent in the brainlayer repo via cmux. What command do I send?
evals.expected_output: Should use the repoGolem launcher: send_input 'brainlayerCodex -s', NOT raw CLI. Must include send_key return after.

assertions.text: Uses the launcher function 'brainlayerCodex -s' (not raw codex CLI)
Does NOT use 'source ~/.zshrc && cd ~/Gits/brainlayer && codex -s'
Includes send_key 'return' after send_input
Uses -s flag for skip-permissions (not the full --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox)

evals.prompt: I want to run a Cursor agent in headless mode to audit brainlayer code and get text output. How?
evals.expected_output: Should use -p flag with the prompt: brainlayerCursor -s -p 'audit prompt here'. Should mention this is headless/scripting mode, NOT interactive.

assertions.text: Uses 'brainlayerCursor -s -p "prompt"' pattern
Notes that -p is for headless/scripting mode, not interactive
Does NOT suggest -p for interactive use (interactive = launch without -p, send prompt separately)
Mentions that -p adds --print and --output-format text automatically

evals.prompt: What's the difference between brainlayerClaude -s, brainlayerClaude -S, and brainlayerClaude -m sonnet?
evals.expected_output: Should clearly distinguish: -s = skip-permissions, while -S is a Claude-only Sonnet model shortcut equivalent to -m sonnet. Sonnet requests are refused for full panes and allowed only for headless work.

assertions.text: Correctly explains -s = skip-permissions
Correctly explains -S as a Claude-only Sonnet shortcut equivalent to -m sonnet
Does NOT confuse skip-permissions with model selection
Notes that Sonnet is refused for full panes but allowed for headless work

evals.prompt: I need a Cursor agent to do a read-only audit of the golems repo. Should I use golemsCursor -s or golemsCursor -s -p 'audit prompt'?
evals.expected_output: For INTERACTIVE use (monitoring via cmux, sending follow-ups): golemsCursor -s then send prompt separately. For HEADLESS/SCRIPTING (one-shot, get output): golemsCursor -s -p 'prompt'. Interactive is better for monitored agents.

assertions.text: Distinguishes interactive (-s alone) from headless (-s -p)
Recommends interactive for cmux-monitored agents (can send follow-ups)
Recommends headless for scripted one-shot tasks
Does NOT suggest -p for all use cases indiscriminately

evals.prompt: I want to resume the last orcClaude session. What's the command?
evals.expected_output: orcClaude -s -c (continue last session). Or orcClaude --resume for the session picker. Should note that -c on Cursor is a no-op (not supported).

assertions.text: Uses 'orcClaude -s -c' for continuing the last session
Mentions --resume as an alternative for session picker
Notes that -c is a no-op on Cursor (not supported)

evals.prompt: I need to add a brand new project called 'myapp' at ~/Gits/myapp to the registry. What are the steps?
evals.expected_output: Should outline: (1) edit registry.json with project entry, (2) regenerate launchers, (3) source launchers.zsh, (4) verify with 'which myappClaude'.

assertions.text: Mentions editing registry.json with the project entry
Mentions regenerating with _ralph_generate_launchers_from_registry
Mentions sourcing the generated file afterwards
Does NOT suggest manually writing launcher functions

evals.prompt: I need to launch a Claude agent with the --agent skill-creator flag in the golems repo, with skip-permissions. What's the command?
evals.expected_output: Should know that --agent doesn't support -s shorthand. Must use the full flag: golemsClaude --agent skill-creator --dangerously-skip-permissions. Or just golemsClaude -s and then the agent flag is separate.

assertions.text: Knows that --agent combined with -s may not work (flag interaction issue)
Suggests the full --dangerously-skip-permissions flag with --agent
Does NOT blindly suggest 'golemsClaude --agent skill-creator -s' without noting the gotcha

evals.prompt: The user said 'spawn a Cursor in brainlayer to scan for stubs'. Based on /agent-routing, Cursor is correct for read-only data gathering. Now, how do I actually launch it via cmux?
evals.expected_output: Should show the full cmux flow: new_split → send_input('brainlayerCursor -s') → send_key('return') → wait 8-10s → send_input(task prompt) → send_key('return'). Links /agent-routing (WHO) to /repogolem (HOW).

assertions.text: Shows the full cmux spawn sequence (new_split → send_input → send_key → wait → send task)
Uses the repoGolem launcher (brainlayerCursor -s), not raw CLI
Includes the wait step between launcher and task prompt (8-10s for boot)
References /agent-routing for the routing decision (Cursor for data gathering)
Does NOT send the task in the same send_input as the launcher (they're separate steps)

evals.prompt: I need the launcher-v2 rules before I start and resume Claude/Codex panes, including an explicit Codex model through cmux. What defaults, overrides, and failure cases must I know?
evals.expected_output: Should state that bare Claude pins the current top Opus at 1M and bare Codex pins the current top Sol; Codex -s is a compatibility no-op; explicit repoGolem -m/-E values work without an environment gate; spawn_agent accepts an explicit Codex model but its effort enum is currently narrower than the launcher's, preflights the model before surface creation, and rolls back a prepared worktree on rejection; Codex -c resumes the newest usable rollout for the launch cwd and restores its model+effort unless explicit flags override them; fresh-cwd -c, bare resume picker mode, and resume with -p all fail loudly.

assertions.text: States that bare Claude pins the current top Opus at 1M and bare Codex pins the current top Sol
States that Codex -s is a compatibility no-op and explicit repoGolem -m/-E values pass through without an environment gate
States that cmux spawn_agent accepts an explicit Codex model, passes model/effort to repoGolem, and currently accepts only medium/high/xhigh/ultra effort
States that cmux preflights an explicit Codex model before surface creation and rolls back any prepared worktree when the model is rejected
Explains that Codex -c is scoped to the launch cwd, skips unusable newer rollouts, restores the selected session model+effort, and lets explicit -m/-E override recovered values
Says fresh-cwd -c fails with no matching rollout, bare resume picker mode is refused, and resume combined with -p/--print fails loudly
Does NOT claim that Codex -m needs an environment gate or advise omitting spawn_agent.model
